items.title: Escape rooms give health care students a safe place to get things wrong
items.summary: The buzzer goes off. Three occupational therapy students are convinced they have worked out what should happen to their patient next. They are wrong.

items.title: Elephants continue to shape the savanna even after death
items.summary: Elephants shape the African savanna. They consume huge amounts of forage, dig for water, topple trees and affect all the animals around them. So, what happens to their outsized presence after these iconic animals pass away?

items.summary: "Photo 51" was a cleaner version of an earlier X-ray image, "Photo 49," that Rosalind Franklin had already used to calculate key features of DNA, challenging long-held assumptions about her role in the discovery of the double helix.

items.summary: Mangrove forests, which are widespread along subtropical and tropical coasts, play a vital role in coastal protection, as they dampen the force of waves and storm surges. They also naturally store carbon in the soil and are home to a wide variety of living organisms.
